subject: Dedicated GPU pool: MAP, eval timeline, pricing & burst scenarios
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir@atlashealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: devops@atlashealth.com, procurement@atlashealth.com
Date: Mon, 08 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Exploring Dedicated GPU pool for Atlas Health — evaluation & timeline

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Atlas Health is evaluating a dedicated GPU pool for our new clinical summarization pipeline. Our initial goals are predictable latency under 150ms p50, and cost predictability for monthly forecasting.

We'd like to run a short eval to validate throughput and latency against a 1M token/day baseline, then pilot for a subset of traffic before a full ramp. Can you share a mutual action plan (MAP) that outlines milestones, expected timelines, and how pricing/commitments interplay with ramp and burst? Procurement will need an initial TCO estimate and proposed term lengths (12/24/36).

Also please include any burst clauses — in particular we need a model for short-term capacity spikes (10-20% of baseline) and how those are priced.

Looking to get an internal decision by mid-February. Who should be on the MAP and can you provide a draft by end of day Wednesday?

Regards,
Samir Rao
Head of ML Platforms
Atlas Health

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@atlashealth.com>
Cc: devops@atlashealth.com, procurement@atlashealth.com
Date: Mon, 08 Feb 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Exploring Dedicated GPU pool for Atlas Health — evaluation & timeline

Samir —

Thanks — appreciate the clarity on objectives. Attached is a first-pass MAP and sizing worksheet to get us started: MAP_v1.0.pdf and GPU_sizing.xlsx. High level proposal below, happy to iterate quickly.

Proposed MAP (high level)
- Week 0–2: Eval (baseline perf + latency tests) — access to a dedicated 4-GPU pool, 2-week test window, Redwood provides a short-run performance profile and tuning support.
- Week 3–6: Pilot (subset of live traffic) — 1-month pilot with 25% traffic window to validate routing and KV cache behavior.
- Month 2–5: Production ramp — staged ramp to 100% over 3 months with agreed checkpoints.

Pricing & commit guidance (draft)
- Reserved slab (monthly commit): options for 12/24/36-month terms. Example starting point: $X per GPU-hour reserved (see GPU_sizing.xlsx for example numbers).
- Ramp discounts: apply 10% discount after 50% committed utilization for >3 months.
- Burst policy: short bursts (up to 20% above reserved baseline) billed at pay-as-you-go rate with a capped monthly spend (we can set a soft cap and alerts). Longer bursts >72 hours will either require transient reservation or a negotiated surcharge.

Next steps
- I'll loop in Sales PE and Pricing for final numbers. Can you confirm procurement contact and the procurement timeline? If you can sign off on the MAP by next Friday (2/12) we can target an order and onboarding the week of 2/22.

Attachments: MAP_v1.0.pdf, GPU_sizing.xlsx

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Cell: (415) 555-0134

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Feb 2027 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pool: MAP, eval timeline, pricing & burst scenarios

Priya — looping Marissa for sizing sanity checks and to propose a pricing matrix. Quoting your note below.

On Mon, Feb 8, 2027 at 11:05 AM Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com> wrote:
> Samir —
>
> Thanks — appreciate the clarity on objectives. Attached is a first-pass MAP and sizing worksheet to get us started: MAP_v1.0.pdf and GPU_sizing.xlsx. High level proposal below, happy to iterate quickly.
>
> Proposed MAP (high level)
> - Week 0–2: Eval (baseline perf + latency tests) — access to a dedicated 4-GPU pool, 2-week test window, Redwood provides a short-run performance profile and tuning support.
> - Week 3–6: Pilot (subset of live traffic) — 1-month pilot with 25% traffic window to validate routing and KV cache behavior.
> - Month 2–5: Production ramp — staged ramp to 100% over 3 months with agreed checkpoints.
>
> Pricing & commit guidance (draft)
> - Reserved slab (monthly commit): options for 12/24/36-month terms. Example starting point: $X per GPU-hour reserved (see GPU_sizing.xlsx for example numbers).
> - Ramp discounts: apply 10% discount after 50% committed utilization for >3 months.
> - Burst policy: short bursts (up to 20% above reserved baseline) billed at pay-as-you-go rate with a capped monthly spend (we can set a soft cap and alerts).

Marking up the proposal:
- Recommend we present three concrete slab options (Small: 4x A100 equiv, Medium: 8x, Large: 16x) with exact per-GPU rates for 12/24/36 month terms.
- For procurement comfort, include an explicit burst SL: 20% free soft-burst per month, then PAGO (pay-as-you-go) up to 50% with a 15% surcharge. Anything beyond 50% requires temporary reservation and 72-hr notice unless escalated.
- Add a termination & migration safety net in SLA-terms.docx (basic data retention and KV-cache handover notes).

I'll attach a working pricing matrix (pricing_matrix_v2.xlsx) and a draft SLA (SLA-terms.docx) to the MAP before sending externally.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@atlashealth.com>
Cc: procurement@atlashealth.com, devops@atlashealth.com
Date: Mon, 14 Feb 2027 16:20:00 -0800
Subject: Final MAP & pricing options — next steps and signature link

Samir —

Appended the updated MAP and pricing as discussed: MAP_v1.0.pdf (annotated), GPU_sizing.xlsx, pricing_matrix_v2.xlsx, and SLA-terms.docx. Key changes since the draft:

- Added three slab options with clear per-GPU-hour rates for 12/24/36-month terms.
- Included a soft-burst allowance: first 20% above reserved baseline free (automatic), PAGO for 20–50% with 15% surcharge, >50% requires temporary reservation or manual escalation.
- Specified ramp discount to kick in after 60 days at sustained 50% utilization (10% reduction).
- Added a migration & termination clause to SLA for safe handover of KV cache and logs.

Target close and onboarding
- If procurement signs the MAP and purchase order by Feb 21, we can schedule onboarding week of Mar 1 and a production ramp plan that reaches 100% in 90 days after onboarding.

Signature link (DocuSign)
- Please review and sign the attached MAP + Order Summary: https://secure.docusign.com/atlas/redwood-rdw-2027
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/5678 (I'll update stages as we progress).

If procurement needs redlines, loop your legal and send us the packet — we can fast-track a redline review.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if you want to walk through the pricing matrix.

Best,
